answer: In a sensor network spanning from an Arctic glacier to the open ocean, agents anchor identities to verifiable observations of a passing comet. By pairing recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments with sequential verifiable delay functions, the system renders identity spoofing computationally infeasible. This cryptographic delay, coupled with staking collateral and slashing penalties, guarantees a negative expected utility for adversaries, establishing a robust Nash equilibrium where Sybil replication is irrational.
